stem.text: The function f gives the height, in meters, of a drone above the ground at time x seconds. The function f is differentiable for all x except \( x = 6 \), where it has a jump discontinuity. Selected values of f are given in the table. Does the Mean Value Theorem guarantee a value c, with \( 4 < c < 8 \), such that \( f'(c) = \frac{3}{4} \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No. Although \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3}{4} \), f is not continuous at \( x = 6 \), which lies in \( \left[4, 8\right] \), so the Mean Value Theorem does not apply and such a c is not guaranteed.

worked_solution.text: The average rate of change of f over \( \left[4, 8\right] \) is \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3 - 0}{4} = \frac{3}{4} \).

The Mean Value Theorem needs f continuous on \( \left[4, 8\right] \) and differentiable on \( (4, 8) \), but f is not continuous at \( x = 6 \), which lies in \( \left[4, 8\right] \). The theorem does not apply, and no other fact given forces \( f'(c) = \frac{3}{4} \) anywhere in the interval, so the answer is no.
worked_solution.rule_named: hypotheses of the Mean Value Theorem

options.label: Yes. Since \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3}{4} \), there is a c with \( 4 < c < 8 \) and \( f'(c) = \frac{3}{4} \), because an average rate of change is always reached by the derivative.
options.derivation: existence asserted from the arithmetic alone, with no theorem named and no check that one applies

options.label: Yes. Since \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3}{4} \), the Mean Value Theorem guarantees such a c, with f taken to be differentiable on \( (4, 8) \).
options.derivation: the Mean Value Theorem applied without checking its hypotheses, which fail at x = 6

options.label: Yes. Since \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3}{4} \), the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees such a c, with f taken to be continuous on \( \left[4, 8\right] \).
options.derivation: the Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative

options.label: No. Although \( \frac{f(8) - f(4)}{8 - 4} = \frac{3}{4} \), f is not continuous at \( x = 6 \), which lies in \( \left[4, 8\right] \), so the Mean Value Theorem does not apply and such a c is not guaranteed.
